questions.def: Singular subject 'quality' requires singular verb 'was'.
questions.question: The quality of the apples ___ poor this year.

questions.def: With 'neither/nor', verb agrees with the closest subject (teacher).
questions.question: Neither the students nor the teacher ___ happy with the test.

questions.def: 'A number' takes a plural verb.
questions.question: A number of students ___ absent today.

questions.def: Subjects like 'mathematics' take a singular verb.
questions.question: Mathematics ___ always been a challenging subject for me.

questions.def: Collective noun 'committee' is plural when acting individually.
questions.question: The committee ___ divided in their opinion.

questions.def: With 'there', verb agrees with the following noun ('reasons').
questions.question: There ___ several reasons for the delay.

questions.def: 'One' is singular, so the verb must be singular.
questions.question: One of my friends ___ studying abroad next year.

questions.def: With uncountable nouns like 'cake', 'all' takes a singular verb.
questions.question: All of the cake ___ eaten.

questions.def: Subject is 'news', an uncountable noun requiring singular verb.
questions.question: What ___ the news about the merger?

questions.def: 'Neither' used alone takes a singular verb.
questions.question: Neither of the options ___ suitable.

questions.def: 'Majority' takes a plural verb when referring to individual members.
questions.question: A majority of voters ___ in favor of the proposal.

questions.def: The team is acting as a single unit so 'is' is correct.
questions.question: The team ___ practicing hard for the finals.

questions.def: 'Many a' takes a singular verb.
questions.question: Many a student ___ struggled with this concept.

questions.def: 'News' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.
questions.question: The news from abroad ___ worrying.

questions.def: 'A pair' takes a singular verb.
questions.question: A pair of shoes ___ on the floor.

questions.def: The subject is 'what' which is singular in this context.
questions.question: What ___ to be done about the issue?

questions.def: 'Species' can be plural, and here it is plural.
questions.question: Several species of birds ___ migrating earlier this year.

questions.def: Subject is 'costs', which is plural, so the verb must be 'are'.
questions.question: The costs associated with travel ___ high.

questions.def: 'Each' before nouns connected by 'and' takes a singular verb.
questions.question: Each boy and girl ___ given a prize.

questions.def: 'The majority' takes a singular verb when referring to a unified opinion.
questions.question: The majority thinks that the plan ___ good.

questions.def: With uncountable nouns, 'rest' takes a singular verb.
questions.question: The rest of the money ___ gone.

questions.def: Indefinite pronouns like 'nobody' are singular.
questions.question: Nobody ___ the answer to the question.

questions.def: 'The number' takes a singular verb.
questions.question: The number of students ___ increasing rapidly.

questions.def: Singular subject 'quality' takes a singular verb 'is'.
questions.question: The quality of these apples ___ not very good.

questions.def: When 'neither/nor' connects subjects, the verb agrees with the closest subject.
questions.question: Neither the students nor the teacher ___ happy with the results.

questions.def: 'Each' is singular, so the verb must be 'has'.
questions.question: Each of the participants have received a certificate of completion.

questions.def: Diseases ending in '-s' that are singular take singular verbs.
questions.question: Measles ___ still a serious disease despite vaccination.

questions.def: 'A number' is plural, so it requires a plural verb: 'are'.
questions.question: A number of students ___ absent today.

questions.def: Expressions like 'along with' don't affect the subject-verb agreement.
questions.question: The CEO, along with her managers, ___ planning the conference.

questions.def: 'What' can be singular; 'seems' agrees with singular 'what'.
questions.question: What ___ to be the problem?
